channel.title: The Crypto Playback
channel.description: Daily research and news on Bitcoin and digital assets, with 24 live market indicators.

item.title: Extreme Fear, Extreme Headlines
item.description: Bitcoin's slide below $58K collided with a wave of regulatory, legal, and infrastructure news that shows the industry building even as the market bleeds.

item.title: Jensen Huang Returns, Bitcoin Catches a Ride on the Coattails
item.description: A wild 48 hours saw Nvidia's CEO drama whipsaw crypto markets while regulators and hackers both chased nine-figure sums through the system.

item.title: Everything Sells Off, Hackers Don't Take a Day Off
item.description: Bitcoin skidded to two-year lows alongside a broader tech wipeout, while a string of DeFi hacks and fresh regulatory moves kept the rest of crypto plenty busy.

item.title: Anthropic Steals the Spotlight, Bitcoin Eats the Spillover
item.description: Wall Street's eyes were on an AI IPO this week, but the crypto market absorbed the shockwaves — with ETF outflows, a death-cross chart pattern, and a stablecoin wobble all landing at once.

item.title: Fed Shock, Miner Sell-Off, and a Billion-Dollar Plea Deal
item.description: Bitcoin slid toward the low $60,000s as a hawkish Fed signal rattled markets, while miners, regulators, and even a German court quietly rewrote the rules of who holds bitcoin and why.

item.title: Bitcoin Can't Hold $65K, Everyone Still Keeps Buying
item.description: Crypto limped through another brutal stretch as Bitcoin flirted with sub-$60K and Ethereum waterfalled lower, even as treasuries, courts, and infrastructure builders kept moving forward regardless.

item.title: Extreme Fear, Extreme Headlines
item.description: Bitcoin slid to multi-month lows and ETF money kept leaving even as regulators, central banks, and tokenization projects quietly kept building out the plumbing underneath.

item.title: Extreme Fear, Extremely Busy DOJ
item.description: Bitcoin slid to multi-week lows alongside Nvidia-driven market jitters, while Washington kept busy seizing billions in hacked crypto and finally naming its crypto regulators.

item.title: Wall Street Keeps Building While Bitcoin Keeps Bleeding
item.description: Institutions are quietly wiring crypto rails into the traditional financial system even as bitcoin's price action stays stuck in a fear-driven rut.

item.title: Wall Street Keeps Tokenizing While Bitcoin Keeps Losing Its Moving Averages
item.description: Institutions keep racing to put stocks on blockchains even as bitcoin itself slides below a key technical level and gets dragged through a billion dollars of liquidations.

item.title: Treasury Swings the Axe, Markets Swing Lower
item.description: Between a $16 billion sanctions hammer, a tech-stock-driven ETF bleed, and Big Tech snubbing crypto's tokenized stock ambitions, this week was less about price and more about who gets to play in the sandbox.

item.title: Fear Dips, Hackers Shuffle, Regulators Circle
item.description: Bitcoin spent the last two days chopping around $75K while Binance's hackers kept moving stolen funds, regulators from Thailand to Nigeria tightened the screws, and Washington inched a 401(k) crypto rule closer to daylig

item.title: Blue Wave Washes Over Crypto Policy as Wall Street Tokenizes Everything
item.description: A Democratic sweep of Congress reshuffled crypto's regulatory odds just as bitcoin clawed back losses and Wall Street kept building on-chain plumbing regardless of who's in charge.

item.title: Hack Hangover Meets Tokenization Pushback
item.description: Crypto is still cleaning up after the Binance hack while a parallel fight over tokenized stocks and a fresh exchange breach in Brazil keep the ledger of bad news growing.

item.title: A $6.3 Billion Wake-Up Call
item.description: The biggest hack in crypto history dominated the week, but a fight over who's really in charge of fixing it may matter more than the number itself.

item.title: Wall Street Keeps Tokenizing, Washington Keeps Stalling
item.description: Bitcoin steadies near $80,500 heading into a Fed decision and the midterms while Wall Street's institutional plumbing — from DTCC to Itaú to Ripple — keeps wiring itself into crypto rails regardless of what Congress does

item.title: Stablecoins Go Mainstream While Washington Sits Still
item.description: While a big bank quietly handed millions of everyday users a stablecoin wallet, Washington's crypto framework stayed stuck and Bitcoin spent the week consolidating under $82,000.

item.title: Stablecoins Everywhere, Bitcoin Nowhere in Particular
item.description: Bitcoin spent the last two days chopping around $81K while the real action happened in ETF filings, stablecoin launches, and a fresh round of code-and-courtroom drama.

item.title: Stablecoins Get a Rulebook, Zcash Gets a Rally
item.description: Regulators finally put pen to paper on stablecoin rules while the market quietly perked up on Zcash's privacy upgrade and a possible Musk mega-merger.

item.title: Banks Go On-Chain While Red Candles Keep Coming
item.description: Wall Street keeps planting flags on public blockchains even as ETF outflows, stablecoin wobbles, and a few ugly hacks remind everyone that crypto's plumbing is still very much under construction.
